event.title: Direct sales recover; March month-end cash report

sources.text: Synthetic scenario document for the Crocs hypothetical private-credit scenario. Management accounts for March 2027, delivered April 16, 2027. Direct-to-consumer sales were 18% above March 2026, helped by spring product that arrived on the rerouted services. Wholesale shipments were 11% below plan.

Synthetic scenario document for the Crocs hypothetical private-credit scenario. Cash report as of March 31, 2027, delivered April 16, 2027. Bank balances across all listed accounts totaled $39.8 million. Of that, $4.1 million is held in a deposit account pledged to secure customs bonds, and $2.1 million is held by Crocs Footwear Retail Asia Pte. Ltd., a fictional entity that is not a Loan Party. No cash was in transit at month-end.

Synthetic scenario document for the Crocs hypothetical private-credit scenario. Wholesale receivables collected in 61 days in March, compared with 46 days at origination, as two customers paid late. As of April 19, 2027 the Lender had not given written notice of any failure to comply.

summary: March 2027 cash fell to $33.6 million, breaching the $35 million minimum cash covenant; receivables slowed to 61 days, weakening the turnover assumption; DTC sales rose 18% while wholesale fell 11%, supporting the DTC offset assumption; monthly reports were delivered on time, satisfying reporting timeliness; the cash shortfall triggers forecast and expansion‑spending restrictions, but no forecast or CAPEX evidence was provided.

attributions.rationale: Unrestricted Cash at March 31 2027 was $33.6 million, below the $50 million forecast floor and the $45 million trigger, contradicting the assumption that cash stays above $50 million.
